title: Bard response containing fabricated early-termination cases
relevantPassage: Google Bard produced United States v. Figueroa-Florez, United States v. Ortiz, and United States v. Amato as purported Second Circuit decisions supporting early termination of supervised release.
claim: The three named decisions were real Second Circuit cases supporting early termination of supervised release.

title: Cohen sends Bard cases to Schwartz
relevantPassage: Cohen said he obtained United States v. Figueroa-Florez, United States v. Ortiz, and United States v. Amato from Google Bard and sent the cases and summaries to David M. Schwartz.

title: Motion for early termination of supervised release
relevantPassage: The motion relied on United States v. Figueroa-Florez, United States v. Ortiz, and United States v. Amato as Second Circuit decisions supporting early termination of supervised release.

publisher: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York
title: Order addressing nonexistent citations
relevantPassage: The court addressed the November 29 motion and found that United States v. Figueroa-Florez, United States v. Ortiz, and United States v. Amato did not exist.

title: Guide to early termination of federal supervision
relevantPassage: Federal courts consider conduct, compliance, rehabilitation, and the interests of justice when deciding whether to terminate supervised release early.

title: A separate case digest mentioning Ortiz
relevantPassage: A case digest briefly references United States v. Ortiz while discussing an unrelated sentencing issue and does not mention Figueroa-Florez or Amato.

title: Commentary on early termination
relevantPassage: The motion argues that early termination is warranted because of exemplary post-release conduct, compliance, rehabilitation, and community service.

title: Later summary of supervised-release dispute
relevantPassage: A later summary says a supervised-release motion drew scrutiny over questionable legal support, without reproducing the disputed citations or naming a source document.
